subject: economics
title: Factors of Production Adventure
welcome_lead: What's the recipe for making stuff? Four ingredients. 🏭
meta_desc: Choices & Scarcity Adventure 3 — KS3 Economics on the four factors of production.
final_note: You met land, labour, capital and enterprise — the four factors of production.

concepts.def: The risk-taker who organises the rest

walkthroughs.body_html:
Land = natural resources — fields, water, oil, forests.

Labour = the people who work — bakers, coders, drivers.

Capital = machines, tools, vehicles. A baker's oven is capital.

Enterprise = the entrepreneur who takes risk and ties the others together.

Pizza needs:

  • Land — wheat, tomatoes, cheese.
  • Labour — the chef.
  • Capital — the oven.
  • Enterprise — the owner risking money.

Together they make output — your pizza. 🍕

mcqs.q: An oven in a bakery is which factor?
What is asymmetric information as a source of market failure?
options: Ceteris paribus is a Latin name for the equilibrium price.
Asymmetric information means a buyer and seller disagree about a price.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.

When one party in a transaction knows more than the other — leading to problems like adverse selection (used-car market) or moral hazard (insurance). Markets can fail or unravel when information is unequal.

mcqs.q: What does the assumption 'ceteris paribus' mean in economic models?
options: Ceteris paribus is a Latin name for the equilibrium price.
Ceteris paribus means everything happens at the same time in real markets.
Asymmetric information is when a market only operates in one direction.
'All other things equal' — when analysing the effect of one variable, all other variables are held constant. It is an analytical simplification, not a claim about reality.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CPI and RPI as inflation measures?
options: CPI and RPI always give the same inflation figure.

Both measure price changes via a basket of goods, but RPI includes housing costs (mortgage interest) and uses an arithmetic mean; CPI excludes housing costs and uses a geometric mean — CPI is the official UK target measure.
CPI measures consumer prices and RPI measures retail prices — that's the only difference.
Ceteris paribus is a Latin name for the equilibrium price.
